The {@code memberId} field carries the owner's current primary 23 * identifier: their unified member id. 24 * 25 * @param seq monotonically increasing sequence number across creates 26 * @param ownerId the persisted owner's id 27 * @param memberId the owner's current primary identifier 28 * @param membershipLevel the owner's membership level 29 * @param event the event type discriminator, always {@link #EVENT_TYPE} 30 */ 31 public record OwnerCreatedEvent(long seq, Integer ownerId, String memberId, int membershipLevel, String event) { 32 33 /** Discriminator value carried by every owner-created event. */ 34 public static final String EVENT_TYPE = "OWNER_CREATED"; 35 36 public OwnerCreatedEvent(long seq, Integer ownerId, String memberId, int membershipLevel) { 37 this(seq, ownerId, memberId, membershipLevel, EVENT_TYPE); 38 } 39 } 40

17	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util;
18	
19	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner;
20	
21	import java.util.Collection;
22	import java.util.OptionalInt;
23	
24	/**
25	 * Derives an owner's {@code membershipLevel} from their scoring fields and applies the
26	 * household level ceiling.
27	 */
28	public final class OwnerMembership {
29	
30	    private OwnerMembership() {
31	    }
32	
33	    /**
34	     * Return the owner's natural (uncapped) membership level, derived purely from their own scoring
35	     * fields via {@link MembershipPointsFormatter} and {@link MembershipLevelFormatter}.
36	     *
37	     * @param owner the owner to score
38	     * @return the membership level, between 1 and 4
39	     */
40	    public static int naturalLevel(Owner owner) {
41	        int points = MembershipPointsFormatter.format(owner.getNamesakeCount(), owner.getEmail(),
42	            owner.getHouseholdSize(), owner.getRegistrationDate());
43	        return MembershipLevelFormatter.format(points);
44	    }
45	
46	    /**
47	     * Return the owner's effective membership level as reported to clients: the capped value stored
48	     * at creation time when present, otherwise the {@link #naturalLevel(Owner) natural level}.
49	     *
50	     * @param owner the owner to score
51	     * @return the membership level, between 1 and 4
52	     */
53	    public static int level(Owner owner) {
54	        return owner.getMembershipLevel() != null ? owner.getMembershipLevel() : naturalLevel(owner);
55	    }
56	
57	    /**
58	     * Return the owner's membership level capped by their household: it may not exceed one above the
59	     * current maximum level among the given existing household members. With no existing member no
60	     * cap applies and the {@link #naturalLevel(Owner) natural level} is returned.
61	     *
62	     * @param owner            the owner being created
63	     * @param householdMembers the existing members of the owner's household (excluding the owner)
64	     * @return the capped membership level, between 1 and 4
65	     */
66	    public static int cappedLevel(Owner owner, Collection<Owner> householdMembers) {
67	        int natural = naturalLevel(owner);
68	        OptionalInt maxMemberLevel = householdMembers.stream()
69	            .mapToInt(OwnerMembership::level)
70	            .max();
71	        return maxMemberLevel.isPresent() ? Math.min(natural, maxMemberLevel.getAsInt() + 1) : natural;
72	    }
73	}

## Summary

The spec: on successful owner create, enqueue a welcome notification by emitting a line via the logger named `NOTIFY` containing the owner id and the memberId.

Changes:

1. **New `WelcomeNotifier` component** (`notification/WelcomeNotifier.java`) — a small, single-responsibility Spring `@Component` that mirrors the existing `OwnerAuditLogger` pattern. It owns a `NOTIFY` SLF4J logger and exposes `welcome(Owner)`, emitting `id=<ownerId> memberId=<memberId>`. Notification concerns stay out of the business logic, just as audit concerns do.

2. **`ClinicServiceImpl`** — injected the `WelcomeNotifier` via the constructor and invoked `welcomeNotifier.welcome(owner)` right after `ownerAuditLogger.ownerCreated(owner)` in `createOwner`, so it fires only on a successful, persisted create (inside the existing `@Transactional` happy path, after all validation/limit checks).

I reused the existing owner id and `memberId` already computed and persisted in the create flow rather than duplicating any logic, and kept each concern in its own unit.
